This video is a part of my collection of traditional tunes that I have learned over the years and because I also teach these tunes I want to make them available to everyone else. This project is very educational for me and handy in teaching-situations. The pictures in each tune are from my photo albums and represents all those fond memories of musical joy. Hope you like it! :)

Fionn’s, X:2

I think that many folk will be playing this lovely tune in D major, especially with flute or whistle players. So here’s the above version transposed.

↳ Posted by Philip W on February 9th, 2025.

Fionn’s, X:3

Here’s roughly how I play this tune in D (with basic chords added), although I probably play it slightly different every time. I first came across it in A and then recently in G, but D is my preferred key.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on February 9th, 2025.

Re: Fionn’s X:2

I have revised this version by copying bars 5 & 6 from Donald K’s version X:3. We do not play those high Es, or equivalent, in bar 5, as played in X:1. Actually I if could, I’d delete this version and leave folk to play Donald K’s version.

↳ Posted by Philip W on March 7th, 2025.
